title: Connascence of Position in Primitive Struct/Method Signatures
pattern: A function takes multiple consecutive parameters of the same primitive type, requiring callers to match the exact positional order.
why_bad: It bypasses compiler type-checking. If a developer swaps the parameters (e.g., passes the seat number as the name), the program compiles successfully but executes completely invalid logic at runtime, producing silent bugs.
detection: A function signature accepts multiple consecutive parameters of the exact same primitive type (e.g., `(String, String)` or `(u32, u32)`).
counterexample: Positional parameters in mathematical coordinates where position is standard and intuitive (e.g., `Point::new(x, y)`).
source: *Mark Richards & Neal Ford - Fundamentals of Software Architecture, Chapter 3 (Modularity), Section "Connascence"*
